overview: White plays 2.b4 against the Symmetrical English, offering a pawn to open the b-file and a-file. After 2...cxb4 3.a3 bxa3 White recaptures with the knight and gets a lead in development and a half-open file on the queenside. Black can keep the pawn but White gets practical play.

white_ideas.idea: Open the queenside with a3 and Nxa3
Use the b2 bishop on the long diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Keep the pawn with ...cxb4 or decline with ...e6
Develop quickly and return it if needed

typical_structures.structure: Open queenside after the b-pawn is traded

gambit.notes: White offers a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.notes: Playable but dubious by most assessments.

character.reason: The gambit invites an open fight with White down a pawn.

gambit.reason: White offers the b-pawn with 2.b4 and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Black can keep the pawn and White's compensation is limited.

structure.reason: The queenside files open but the centre stays fixed.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose the Wing Gambit.

level.reason: Dubious means not Beginner, and the ideas are straightforward.

plans.reason: The gambit pawn buys White quick development and the b-file.
